summary: Temozolomide is an oral alkylating agent for newly diagnosed glioblastoma (with radiotherapy then maintenance) and anaplastic astrocytoma. Concomitant dose is 75 mg/m2/day; maintenance is 150-200 mg/m2 on days 1-5 of 28-day cycles. Myelosuppression is dose-limiting; hepatotoxicity and PCP risk require monitoring and prophylaxis.
indications: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, concomitantly with radiotherapy and then as maintenance treatment
Adjuvant treatment of adults with newly diagnosed anaplastic astrocytoma
Treatment of adults with refractory anaplastic astrocytoma

dosage.d: 75 mg/m2 once daily for 42-49 days with focal radiotherapy
150 mg/m2 once daily on Days 1-5 of a 28-day cycle
May increase to 200 mg/m2 Days 1-5 if tolerated
dosage.n: Based on toxicity; up to 6 cycles

dosage.d: Initial 150 mg/m2 Days 1-5 every 28 days; may increase to 200 mg/m2

admin: Administer orally or intravenously; take oral capsules consistently, preferably on an empty stomach to reduce nausea/vomiting
Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open or chew - avoid skin/mucosal contact with contents
Provide PCP prophylaxis during the concomitant phase and continue in lymphopenic patients until recovery
Check ANC and platelets before each cycle and on Day 22 / weekly as required; adjust dose for toxicity
moa: A prodrug that undergoes rapid nonenzymatic conversion at physiologic pH to the active alkylating species MTIC. MTIC methylates DNA primarily at the O6 and N7 positions of guanine. The cytotoxic O6-methylguanine lesion causes futile mismatch repair cycles and DNA strand breaks, triggering apoptosis. Tumors with low MGMT activity are more sensitive.

absolute: History of severe hypersensitivity to temozolomide
Hypersensitivity to dacarbazine (DTIC) - shares MTIC metabolite

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism of action and animal studies; postmarketing reports include spontaneous abortions and congenital malformations. Contraindicated in pregnancy; advise effective contraception for patients and male partners during and after treatment.
lact: Discontinue breastfeeding during treatment and for a period after the last dose due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant.
renal: Use with caution; pharmacokinetics in severe renal impairment are not well studied. Monitor closely.
hepatic: Use with caution; fatal and severe hepatotoxicity have been reported. Perform liver tests at baseline, midway through the first cycle, before each subsequent cycle, and 2-4 weeks after the last dose.

major: Live vaccines - risk of disseminated infection in immunosuppressed patients
Other myelosuppressive agents - additive marrow toxicity
moderate: Valproic acid - slightly decreases temozolomide clearance
interactions.food: Food reduces the rate and extent of absorption; take consistently, preferably on an empty stomach, and use antiemetics.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes myelosuppression (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, lymphopenia) and may elevate liver enzymes.

serious: Pneumocystis pneumonia and other opportunistic infections

monitoring: Complete blood count with platelets before each cycle, on Day 22 and weekly until recovery
Liver function tests at baseline, mid-first-cycle, before each cycle and 2-4 weeks after last dose
Signs of infection, especially Pneumocystis pneumonia in lymphopenic patients
counsel: Take capsules whole, consistently, preferably on an empty stomach with water
Do not open or crush capsules; avoid contact with skin or eyes
Report fever, signs of infection, unusual bruising or bleeding promptly
Use effective contraception during and after treatment; do not breastfeed
Take prescribed anti-nausea and PCP prophylaxis medications
pk: Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect capsules from moisture
pearls: Myelosuppression is dose-limiting - geriatric patients and women are at higher risk; check counts before each cycle.
Provide PCP prophylaxis during concomitant radiotherapy phase; continue while lymphopenic.
Hepatotoxicity can be fatal - monitor liver tests on the defined schedule.
MGMT promoter methylation status predicts greater benefit.
missed: If a daily dose is missed, do not take a double dose; contact the oncology team for guidance, as missed days can affect the cycle. Resume per the prescribed schedule under clinician direction.
overdose: Dose-limiting toxicity is hematologic; overdose can cause severe and prolonged myelosuppression and infection. There is no specific antidote. Provide supportive care with blood count monitoring, growth factors/transfusions and treatment of infection or bleeding.
